description: This bar chart visually categorizes five distinct patterns of parameter-efficient fine-tuning design spaces, each represented by a horizontal bar plot with five bars per category. The horizontal axis serves as the category label axis, displaying the names “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Bottleneck,” and a fifth unlabeled category with a gray bar placeholder. The vertical axis represents the value axis, which is unlabeled and lacks a defined scale or unit, but the height of each bar corresponds to a quantitative measure of the design space's characteristics. For the “Increasing” pattern, the bars rise progressively from left to right, with approximate heights of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5. The “Uniform” pattern shows five bars of equal height, approximately 0.3 each. The “Decreasing” pattern displays bars that fall progressively from left to right, with approximate heights of 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, and 0.1. The fourth category, visually represented by a gray bar placeholder, lacks a label and thus its pattern cannot be described. The “Bottleneck” pattern features bars of varying heights, with approximate values of 0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4. All bars are rendered in a uniform light green color, and none are sorted or visually emphasized beyond their positional arrangement within each group.
